# Project Backlog - Restaurant Waitlist & Table Manager

This backlog contains the development tasks required to build the Restaurant Waitlist & Table Manager web application. Each task is self-contained, independent, and designed to fit in a single session.

---

## 1. Project Initialization & Passing Test
Goal: Scaffold the React frontend and FastAPI backend directories and verify the environment with a passing test in each.
Description: Create the repository structure containing a `backend/` directory with a minimal FastAPI app and a `frontend/` directory with a standard React TypeScript project. Configure simple test environments for both (pytest for Python and Vitest/Jest for React) and write a single, basic assertion test in each that runs and passes successfully.

## 2. Database Models and Migration Setup
Goal: Define the SQLite database schema and SQLAlchemy ORM models for waitlist, tables, and SMS log entities.
Description: Define SQLAlchemy schemas for `tables` (columns: id, name, capacity, status, current_party_id), `waitlist` (columns: id, guest_name, party_size, phone_number, status, joined_at, notified_at, seated_at, table_id), and `sms_logs` (columns: id, phone_number, message, sent_at). Create a database initialization script inside the backend that creates these tables on startup and populates a set of default table structures (e.g., Table 1 to 10 with various capacities) to facilitate local testing.

## 3. Waitlist CRUD REST APIs
Goal: Build the backend endpoints for guests to join the waitlist and hosts to modify guest status.
Description: Implement FastAPI REST endpoints for `POST /api/waitlist` (add guest with status WAITING), `GET /api/waitlist` (fetch active waiting parties), `PUT /api/waitlist/{id}/status` (update status to NOTIFIED, SEATED, or CANCELLED), and `DELETE /api/waitlist/{id}` (remove guest). Ensure the endpoints write database changes through SQLAlchemy, return appropriate JSON payloads, and include comprehensive unit tests validating state transitions.

## 4. Table Management REST APIs
Goal: Build backend endpoints to manage physical restaurant tables and assign guests.
Description: Implement FastAPI endpoints `GET /api/tables` to retrieve all tables with their occupancy statuses and `POST /api/tables/{id}/clear` to set an occupied table status back to DIRTY or AVAILABLE. Implement a `POST /api/waitlist/{party_id}/seat` endpoint that validates that a party's size fits within the chosen table's capacity, updates the table status to OCCUPIED with the party ID, and changes the waitlist party status to SEATED.

## 5. Real-Time WebSocket Notification System
Goal: Set up a WebSocket endpoint and broadcaster to synchronize state changes instantly.
Description: Implement an asynchronous WebSocket manager in FastAPI that listens at `/ws` and tracks active host and guest connections. Write utility methods to broadcast a text or JSON message (e.g., "QUEUE_UPDATE" or "TABLE_UPDATE") to all active clients whenever a guest joins, gets notified, is seated, or a table is cleared, enabling instant updates on the frontend.

## 6. Staff PIN Verification & Navigation
Goal: Implement a simple staff PIN access system in the React application to separate guest and staff views.
Description: Build a secure-looking lock screen modal in React that requests a 4-digit PIN (defaulting to `1234`) and stores a session authorization token when entered correctly. Integrate this logic into a high-level navigation router so that only successfully authenticated users can access the Host Dashboard, while unauthorized attempts redirect to the Guest views.

## 7. Waitlist Queue Dashboard UI
Goal: Build the host dashboard view for managing active waiting parties and triggering alerts.
Description: Create a React grid-layout table displaying the active waitlist queue sorted chronologically by arrival time. Add interactive action buttons to each row: a "Notify" button (which sends a request to the server, triggers a mock text, and flashes a visual indicator) and a "Seat" button (which prompts a modal showing available tables) to allow hosts to manage guest flow easily.

## 8. Interactive Table Map UI
Goal: Create a visual, responsive grid layout of the restaurant's physical tables for the host.
Description: Build a visual grid component in React displaying individual cards/shapes representing each physical table in the database, color-coded by current status: Green (Available), Red (Occupied, showing party name and size), and Yellow (Dirty). Include interactive action controls on each table card, such as clicking an "Available" table to manually occupy it, or clicking a "Dirty" table to mark it "Clean" (Available).

## 9. Self-Service Guest Registration Form
Goal: Design a clean, mobile-optimized page for guests to join the waitlist.
Description: Build a mobile-friendly page at `/guest/join` containing a simple registration form with fields for Guest Name, Party Size, and Phone Number. On submit, send a POST request to the backend waitlist API, handle success/error states, and redirect the guest automatically to their personal live tracking page.

## 10. Real-Time Guest Status Tracker
Goal: Build a live tracking page for guests to monitor their position and receive notifications.
Description: Create a mobile-first page at `/guest/track/{party_id}` that displays the party's current status, estimated remaining wait time, and a dynamic progress bar. Connect to the WebSocket endpoint to receive live broadcast alerts, immediately updating the page or displaying a large banner when the host clicks "Notify" for their party.

## 11. Integrated Mock SMS Logger UI
Goal: Build a localized mock SMS inbox window for developers to view sent text notifications in real-time.
Description: Create a collapsible drawer or side-panel component in the application's interface that fetches and displays the latest entries from the `sms_logs` table. Ensure that whenever the backend generates a text notification (e.g., "Your table is ready!"), the mock logger automatically updates to show the message body, phone number, andtimestamp, enabling seamless local testing of the complete flow.
